newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Sanctions no bar to Burma's ASEAN entry-Mahathir.
newsitem.headline: Sanctions no bar to Burma's ASEAN entry-Mahathir.

text.p: Malaysia's prime minister said on Wednesday U.S. sanctions would not delay the entry of Burma into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Asked by reporters if Washington's economic sanctions would hold back Burma's admission into the regional grouping, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said: "No, no, no."

A spokesman for Mahathir later confirmed the prime minister said he did not see the sanctions disrupting Burma's entry into ASEAN. Malaysia is currently the chairman of ASEAN, which also includes Brunei, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
"We're going to work very hard to get Myanmar (Burma) into ASEAN," Mahathir said.

The United States said on Tuesday it would ban new investment by American firms in Burma because of what Washington described as deepening political repression by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
ASEAN will decide by July whether to admit Burma, along with Cambodia and Laos, as new members.

Mahathir, stopped by reporters after a luncheon speech to businessmen, was asked if Malaysia would protest the sanctions in its capacity as ASEAN chairman. "We'll talk with other ASEAN ministers," he said.
Asked if ASEAN's ties with Washington would be affected, he said: "I don't know. I can't predict what ASEAN will say."
Some diplomats believe the latest sanctions would add to the considerable international pressure on ASEAN not to admit Burma.
But the group says it follows a policy of "constructive engagement" with Rangoon and never interferes in the politics of another nation.
